explanation: A burn directly harms the physical tissues of the body, making it a physical stressor. The others are mental or social stressors!

question: A patient arrives at the ward struggling to breathe with swollen legs from heart failure. Which drug type is best to give right away for quick relief?

options.A: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
options.B: Potassium-sparing diuretic
options.C: Loop diuretic
options.D: Osmotic diuretic

explanation: When you need fast, powerful fluid removal in an emergency like severe swelling or breathing trouble, loop diuretics are your go-to choice!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason why patients struggle to sleep in a hospital?

options.A: Comfortable room temperatures and soft lighting
options.B: Physical pain and post-operative discomfort
options.C: Frequent nighttime vital sign checks by staff
options.D: Constant noise from equipment and hallway chatter

explanation: Hospitals are usually noisy, bright, and busy with checks—not exactly a peaceful spa! Comfortable conditions actually help patients sleep.

question: Which blood-borne pathogen carries the highest risk of infection after just a single accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B has a very high concentration in the blood, making it the most easily transmitted pathogen following a needle-stick accident.

question: What is a dangerous storage practice that often leads to accidental poisoning?

options.A: Using weekly pill boxes for daily vitamins
options.B: Keeping medicines in a locked bathroom cabinet
options.C: Leaving laundry detergent pods high on a shelf
options.D: Putting cleaning chemicals in old beverage bottles

explanation: Storing chemicals in food or drink containers tricks children and adults into thinking the liquid is safe to consume. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which children's condition often needs rectal washouts before surgery?

options.A: Hirschsprung's disease
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Congenital heart failure
options.D: Infantile jaundice

explanation: In Hirschsprung's disease, a part of the baby's bowel lacks the nerves to push stool out. Washouts are safely used to clear things out before surgery!

question: Why is it sometimes a bad idea to immediately stop infectious diarrhoea with medicine?

options.A: It permanently destroys the muscles of the colon
options.B: It completely stops the absorption of all vitamins
options.C: It traps harmful toxins and bacteria inside the gut
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When germs cause diarrhoea, your body tries to flush them out. Stopping the flow too soon just keeps the bad stuff trapped inside you!

question: What is the nurse's main role when it comes to informed consent?

options.A: Writing the medical prescription for the diagnostic procedure
options.B: Explaining the legal liability of the hospital to the family
options.C: Deciding whether the patient is well enough to undergo the test
options.D: Ensuring the patient understands the procedure and has signed voluntarily

explanation: Well done! The nurse makes sure the patient truly gets what the doctor explained and is agreeing of their own free will—no pressure!

question: Why do heart conditions often lead to dangerous electrical rhythm problems?

options.A: The brain sends extra electricity to the chest on purpose
options.B: Heart valves open and close too softly
options.C: Red blood cells carry too much oxygen to the nodes
options.D: Damaged or scarred heart muscle messes up normal electrical pathways

explanation: Electricity needs a smooth road to travel. When scar tissue or lack of oxygen damages the heart muscle, the electrical signals get blocked or go haywire, causing erratic heartbeats.

question: Why do nurses need to understand basic physical therapy principles?

options.A: To reinforce exercises during daily patient care activities
options.B: To diagnose musculoskeletal disorders independently
options.C: To replace the work of physical therapists on the ward
options.D: To prescribe new rehabilitation programs for patients

explanation: You spend the most time with patients on the ward! By understanding these basics, you can help patients keep up with their exercises while doing normal daily care.

question: Which germ causes oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Oral thrush is a fungal infection that happens when Candida albicans grows a bit too much in the mouth.

question: Why is soluble fiber often recommended in the dietary management of faecal incontinence?

options.A: It relaxes the internal sphincter muscle
options.B: It completely stops all digestive activity in the stomach
options.C: It absorbs excess water to form a firmer, more formed stool
options.D: It prevents the absorption of all dietary fats

explanation: Soluble fiber adds bulk and consistency to liquid or loose stools, making them much easier for the sphincters to control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which medication class is well-known for causing severe constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Short-acting diuretics
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilators

explanation: Opioids slow down the movement of the gastrointestinal tract significantly, leading to hard, difficult-to-pass stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when starting community mobilisation?

options.A: Entry and sensitization with local leaders
options.B: Building a brand new brick health clinic
options.C: Punishing people who miss immunization days
options.D: Writing the final project evaluation report

explanation: You must enter respectfully and introduce yourself to leaders before trying to assess needs or plan actions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which dimension of health involves the ability to handle daily stress and express feelings properly?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Emotional dimension
options.C: Intellectual dimension
options.D: Environmental dimension

explanation: The emotional dimension focuses on mental resilience, coping mechanisms, and emotional expression. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: A dying patient says they are scared to die alone while family steps out. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because family will be back tomorrow
options.B: Sit with them and offer a reassuring, calming presence
options.C: Run out to find the doctor right away
options.D: Tell them to think about happier times

explanation: Sometimes your physical presence is the best medicine. Just staying by their side chases away that terrifying loneliness.

question: What is the main functional challenge when a patient has a congenitally shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: The time window for optimal gamete interaction and transport is compressed
options.B: Progesterone production by the tubal mucosa is permanently doubled
options.C: Sperm are completely blocked from entering the peritoneal cavity
options.D: Ovulation is prevented from occurring on the affected side

explanation: A shorter tube means less time and space for the delicate timing needed between sperm meeting the egg and the egg traveling down safely.

question: Why is post-test counselling still very important for someone who tests negative?

options.A: To prepare them for inevitable immune system decline
options.B: To reinforce prevention strategies and help them stay negative
options.C: To counsel them on managing chronic medication side effects
options.D: To verify that they paid the laboratory testing fee in full

explanation: Brilliant! A negative result is a great teaching moment to talk about safe habits, PrEP, and keeping that negative status.

question: Why can crossing the legs during a blood pressure check lead to a falsely high reading?

options.A: It blocks blood flow completely in the arm's brachial artery
options.B: It increases physical tension and blood vessel resistance in the body
options.C: It stops the machine from pumping air into the cuff
options.D: It drains the battery of the electronic device faster

explanation: Crossed legs and slouching temporarily boost your vascular pressure. Always remind patients to uncross their legs and keep feet flat on the floor!

question: What vital paper must always travel with a critically ill patient during a transfer?

options.A: A blank sheet of paper for the driver to take notes on
options.B: A detailed referral note outlining history, vital signs, and treatments given
options.C: The personal identity card of the attending nurse
options.D: A receipt for the purchase of hospital drugs

explanation: The receiving team needs to know what happened so far, what vital signs look like, and what drugs were given.

question: A patient scheduled for discharge is crying and upset after a new diagnosis. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Postpone detailed instructions until the patient's emotional readiness improves
options.B: Ask a family member to take over all future health responsibilities
options.C: Hand the patient a textbook and tell them to read it alone
options.D: Proceed quickly with the teaching so the patient leaves on time

explanation: Well reasoned! High emotions block learning. Comforting the patient and waiting until they are calmer is always the right clinical call.

question: What is the best next step for a patient who comes back with a strongly positive Mantoux test?

options.A: Discharge the patient with instructions to return next year
options.B: Refer the patient for a chest X-ray and clinical evaluation
options.C: Immediately start a full course of multi-drug TB treatment
options.D: Administer a second booster Mantoux test on the other arm

explanation: A positive skin test is a warning sign, not a final diagnosis. We always send them for a chest X-ray to check if their lungs are clear or if the infection is active. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in our body?

options.A: Defending the body against foreign pathogens
options.B: Regulating body functions through hormone secretion
options.C: Filtering waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.D: Providing structural support for internal organs

explanation: Think of the endocrine system as your body's chemical messaging network! It uses glands to release hormones straight into the blood, controlling everything from growth to metabolism. You've got this!

question: In young children with sickle cell anaemia, what is dactylitis?

options.A: Severe infection of the lung tissue
options.B: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.C: Sudden yellowing of the eyes and skin
options.D: Abnormal enlargement of the liver

explanation: Dactylitis is often one of the very first signs of sickle cell disease in babies. It happens when sickled cells block blood flow in the tiny bones of the hands and feet, causing painful swelling.

question: Why do we prefer tube feeding (enteral nutrition) over drip feeding into a vein (parenteral nutrition) if the gut is working?

options.A: It lets the patient eat regular meals at the same time
options.B: It is much cheaper and needs no equipment
options.C: It has zero risk of infection
options.D: It keeps the gut lining healthy and prevents it from wasting away

explanation: Use it or lose it! Keeping food moving through the GI tract keeps the intestinal walls strong and stops bad bacteria from leaking out.

question: What is the immediate action needed for a patient in acute urinary retention?

options.A: Administration of oral diuretic medications
options.B: Application of warm compresses to the lower back
options.C: Immediate open surgical removal of the prostate gland
options.D: Urinary catheterization to relieve bladder distension

explanation: When a patient cannot pass urine and is in agonizing pain, the immediate fix is draining the bladder safely with a urinary catheter.

question: Which of these tasks is usually handled by a nursing assistant rather than a Registered Nurse (RN)?

options.A: Assisting with daily bathing and dressing
options.B: Creating the master patient care plan
options.C: Administering intravenous medications
options.D: Diagnosing new chronic health conditions

explanation: Nursing assistants are fantastic at providing direct, hands-on personal care to keep patients comfortable and clean every day.

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE systematic assessment approach?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Bleeding

explanation: In the ABCDE emergency assessment framework, B stands for evaluating the patient's breathing status and chest movement. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: As a nurse assisting with an ultrasound-guided needle procedure, what is your most important duty?

options.A: Adjusting the machine's sound frequency during the scan
options.B: Keeping the area strictly sterile and helping the patient stay still
options.C: Giving the patient general anesthesia
options.D: Reading and writing the final report

explanation: Invasive bedside procedures need strict infection control and a steady patient to keep everything safe and accurate.

question: Which common side effect often occurs due to the stimulant properties of bronchodilators like albuterol?

options.A: Rapid heart rate and palpitations
options.B: Uncontrollable drowsiness and sleep
options.C: Severe drop in blood pressure
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of taste

explanation: Beta-agonist bronchodilators stimulate heart receptors, frequently causing a fast heartbeat or jittery feeling. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the major danger if a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) breaks free from a leg vein?

options.A: It can travel to the lungs and cause a pulmonary embolism.
options.B: It reverses blood flow and causes high blood pressure.
options.C: It will dissolve harmlessly inside the liver tissues.
options.D: It causes immediate gangrene in the toes of that foot.

explanation: A loose clot becomes a travelling troublemaker (embolus), riding the bloodstream straight into the lungs where it can block vital blood flow.

question: Which of these is NOT a good idea if you are facing backlash or resistance for your advocacy work?

options.A: Building strong community alliances
options.B: Relying strictly on verified factual data
options.C: Collaborating with professional nursing bodies
options.D: Acting completely alone without informing anyone

explanation: Correct! Trying to fight battles all by yourself puts you at high risk. True safety and strength always come from teamwork and professional support.

question: Which gas law explains why trapped air inside a patient's body expands as an aircraft climbs?

options.A: Dalton's Law
options.B: Henry's Law
options.C: Newton's Law
options.D: Boyle's Law

explanation: Think of Boyle's Law: pressure and volume are opposites! When cabin pressure drops at high altitudes, trapped body gases expand. You'll master this physics connection in no time.

question: A patient with Pick's disease tries to eat paper wrappers and craves tons of sugar. How should you understand this?

options.A: It indicates the patient is suffering from severe iron-deficiency anemia.
options.B: It is a typical oral and dietary manifestation caused by temporal lobe damage.
options.C: It is a deliberate attempt by the patient to seek attention from staff.
options.D: It proves the patient has developed a secondary bacterial throat infection.

explanation: When the temporal lobe is affected, patients often develop strange eating habits, like craving sweets or trying to swallow non-food items. It's not for attention—it's the disease at work!

question: A 15-year-old girl is admitted to the clinic with severe birth complications from an early pregnancy. What should be the nurse's immediate priority?

options.A: Provide urgent medical stabilization while ensuring a safe, confidential environment
options.B: Focus entirely on billing procedures before initiating physical examinations
options.C: Scold the family in the waiting room for breaking child protection laws
options.D: Refuse to treat the patient until local police officers arrive at the bedside

explanation: You're a natural! A nurse's absolute first priority is always immediate clinical care and creating a safe, trustworthy space for a vulnerable patient.

question: Which nursing action is best for preventing constipation in an immobile bedbound patient?

options.A: Administering a strong daily enema before breakfast
options.B: Encouraging fluids, high-fiber foods, and passive or active movement
options.C: Telling the patient to hold bowel movements until evening
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to slow down digestion

explanation: Combining hydration, fiber, and physical movement addresses the main lifestyle causes of constipation safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: How is spongy bone different from compact bone?

options.A: It lacks a blood supply entirely
options.B: It is made completely of soft cartilage
options.C: It is found only on the outer surface of long bones
options.D: It has a porous, web-like structure instead of solid layers

explanation: Spot on! Spongy bone looks a bit like a honeycomb with little struts (trabeculae), making it lightweight, while compact bone is super solid and dense.

question: How do newborn babies mostly make body heat when they get cold?

options.A: Through vigorous involuntary shivering
options.B: By metabolizing brown adipose tissue
options.C: By activating sweat gland secretions
options.D: Through rapid skeletal muscle contraction

explanation: Babies can't shiver like adults do! Instead, they burn a special kind of fat called brown fat (adipose tissue) to stay warm. It's a neat trick, but it uses up a lot of energy.

question: You notice an unresponsive patient has noisy, gurgling breathing. What should be your very first nursing action?

options.A: Administer a dose of intravenous glucose
options.B: Document the Glasgow Coma Scale score
options.C: Suction the airway to clear secretions
options.D: Apply warm blankets to prevent shivering

explanation: Well done! Gurgling means fluid or spit is blocking the airway, so clearing it out takes priority over everything else.

question: Which of these actions goes against professional nursing ethics in the workplace?

options.A: Providing emergency first aid to a worker who cut their hand
options.B: Disclosing an employee's private medical diagnosis to management without consent
options.C: Educating staff members on proper manual lifting techniques
options.D: Reporting a dangerous chemical spill to the company safety officer

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing a worker's private medical details with bosses without permission is a serious breach of nursing ethics.

question: Why should we avoid giving strong painkillers before a doctor figures out the exact cause of a severe tummy ache?

options.A: It stops the kidneys from making urine
options.B: It immediately drops the patient's blood pressure
options.C: It always damages the stomach lining
options.D: It can hide warning signs of a surgical emergency like a burst organ

explanation: Pain is actually a helpful clue! If painkillers wipe it out completely, doctors might miss critical signs that a patient urgently needs surgery.

question: Right after birth, during which psychological phase does a new mother focus heavily on herself and rely on others for decisions?

options.A: Taking-in phase
options.B: Letting-go phase
options.C: Taking-hold phase
options.D: Depressive phase

explanation: Great thinking! In the 'taking-in' phase right after delivery, the mum is resting, processing her birth story, and letting nurses and family take care of her needs.

question: What common physical thing inside the rectum can block a drug from working well?

options.A: Presence of a fecal mass
options.B: Excessive stomach acid
options.C: High levels of oral saliva
options.D: Dehydration of the skin

explanation: Stool in the way prevents the suppository from touching the bowel wall so it can melt and absorb properly.

question: You are planning meals for a low-income family with a malnourished toddler. What is the best action?

options.A: Tell the family to fast for two days to clean the child's stomach
options.B: Recommend affordable, locally available foods for nutritious meals
options.C: Send the child for long-term admission in an expensive private hospital
options.D: Insist they buy costly imported baby milk from the city

explanation: Well done! Care plans must be practical and use cheap local foods that actually fit the family's financial pocket.

question: Which physical assessment technique is used to check for kidney tenderness at the back?

options.A: Inspection
options.B: Percussion
options.C: Retraction
options.D: Auscultation

explanation: Great job! Gently tapping (percussing) the costovertebral angle at the back helps us check if the kidneys are inflamed or tender.

question: How often should a nurse routinely inspect a standard peripheral intravenous site?

options.A: At least once every nursing shift
options.B: Once every three days when fluids finish
options.C: Every time the patient eats a meal
options.D: Only when the infusion pump starts beeping

explanation: Regular checks catch early signs of complications like swelling, redness, or leaking before they turn severe. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h7)

question: How should a nurse handle personal religious beliefs when faced with an emergency PAC case?

options.A: By prioritizing the immediate life-saving care and treating the client without judgment
options.B: By transferring the patient to another facility without stabilization
options.C: By lecturing the client on morality before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: By refusing to touch the patient until a religious leader speaks with her

explanation: In an emergency, saving a patient's life and providing compassionate nursing care always comes before personal opinions.

question: Your surgical mask becomes damp and sweaty during a busy shift. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it on because moisture helps filtration
options.B: Flip it inside out so the dry side faces out
options.C: Remove and discard it, clean your hands, and put on a fresh one
options.D: Wipe it with paper towels and pocket it

explanation: Once a mask gets damp, its filter barrier stops working well. Swap it out for a fresh one to stay safe!

question: What physical sign should a nurse check for when assessing a patient for fluid overload due to excess salt intake?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Pitting edema in the ankles and shins
options.C: Extreme dryness and cracking of the lips
options.D: Rapid thinning of the fingernail beds

explanation: Fluid retention from excess sodium pooling in the lower extremities commonly presents as pitting edema over bony prominences. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h8)

question: How do calcimimetic medications help treat hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: They stimulate the thyroid gland to produce more calcitonin.
options.B: They block vitamin D receptors in the gut to stop food absorption.
options.C: They make the parathyroid glands more sensitive to calcium, lowering PTH release.
options.D: They dissolve kidney stones quickly by breaking down calcium deposits.

explanation: Calcimimetics trick the parathyroid cells into feeling like there's plenty of calcium around, so they slow down and release less PTH.

question: Why do children get medication doses calculated by body weight instead of a standard adult dose?

options.A: Children metabolize all drugs faster than adult patients
options.B: Children have developing organ systems and varying body sizes
options.C: Liquid medications always require weight-based measurements
options.D: Standard adult doses are illegal to give to anyone under age twelve

explanation: Kids aren't just tiny adults! Because their little bodies and metabolic organs are still growing, weight-based dosing keeps them safe from accidental overdoses.

question: What is the main goal of debulking surgery for ovarian cancer?

options.A: To preserve the uterus and ovaries for future childbearing
options.B: To completely cure the patient without needing chemotherapy
options.C: To remove as much visible tumor mass from the abdomen as possible
options.D: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests

explanation: Spot on! Leaving behind as little tumor as possible makes the follow-up chemotherapy much more effective.

question: Which medication is often given alongside NSAIDs to stop pericarditis from coming back?

options.A: Warfarin
options.B: Digoxin
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Colchicine

explanation: Colchicine works brilliantly alongside NSAIDs to calm down stubborn inflammation and prevent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is formed right after a sperm successfully fertilizes an egg?

options.A: An unfertilized follicle
options.B: A diploid zygote
options.C: A mature blastocyst
options.D: A haploid gamete

explanation: When the sperm and egg join, they combine their chromosomes to restore a full set of 46, creating a brand new single-celled zygote ready to grow!

question: How do doctors usually confirm a diagnosis of Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: An electrical muscle test of the upper and lower limbs
options.B: A simple finger-prick blood glucose test done at the bedside
options.C: Clinical history, neurological assessment, and neuroimaging
options.D: A 24-hour urine collection measuring total protein content

explanation: Since there isn't one quick blood test for it, clinicians look at the patient's story, test their memory, and use brain scans like an MRI.

question: Which of these conditions is a classic reason to use a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute sinusitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Spot on! Sinusitis brings painful inflammation and blocked nasal passages, which respond wonderfully to the warm, soothing moisture of steam therapy.

question: If your rural clinic runs out of official safety boxes, what is a safe, clever backup plan for used needles?

options.A: Using locally available, puncture-resistant rigid containers
options.B: Throwing loose needles directly into the regular dustbin
options.C: Burying uncapped needles in the hospital garden
options.D: Washing and reusing disposable needles for multiple patients

explanation: Improvise safely! Using a sturdy, thick local container keeps everyone safe from needle pricks until official disposal arrives.

question: What is the medical term for abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Oligomenorrhea
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia describes periods that are excessively heavy or last longer than normal, often draining the body's iron stores. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is it better for nurses to advocate together through an organization rather than fighting alone at the bedside?

options.A: It removes the legal duty of care from individual practitioners
options.B: It prevents hospital management from ever questioning a nurse
options.C: It guarantees that all patient complaints are immediately dismissed
options.D: It gives nurses a stronger political voice to influence health laws

explanation: Politicians and policy-makers listen much more closely to an organized group representing thousands of healthcare workers than to a single voice!

question: What is the ultimate goal of patient education when teaching someone how to care for their diabetes at home?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever experiencing normal life stress
options.B: Eliminating all future visits to the primary healthcare clinic
options.C: Empowering the patient to safely manage their daily condition
options.D: Ensuring the family takes complete control of medication administration

explanation: Good education gives patients the tools, knowledge, and confidence to take charge of their own health every day. Love to see it!

question: Which of these body fluids has a high enough viral concentration to transmit HIV?

options.A: Saliva
options.B: Breast milk
options.C: Tears
options.D: Sweat

explanation: Breast milk can transmit HIV, unlike casual contact fluids like sweat, tears, or saliva. Great job!

question: Why do nurses place an unconscious, breathing patient into the lateral recovery position?

options.A: To stop the patient from experiencing painful muscle spasms
options.B: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway and reduce the risk of aspiration
options.C: To increase blood flow directly to the frontal lobes of the cerebrum
options.D: To make it easier for nurses to check blood pressure every hour

explanation: Great thinking! Gravity helps pull saliva or vomit away from the airway when they lie safely on their side.

question: What is the best way to prevent accidental needlestick injuries after giving an injection?

options.A: Carefully placing the plastic cap back onto the needle using two hands.
options.B: Dropping the uncapped needle directly into a rigid sharps box.
options.C: Leaving the used syringe on the bedside table until the end of the shift.
options.D: Breaking the needle off the syringe before throwing it in the trash.

explanation: Great job! Never try to recap a used needle—that is the number one cause of accidental pricks. Drop it straight into the safety box!

question: Why must you be extra careful when trying to use the basilic vein for venepuncture?

options.A: It lies close to the brachial artery and median nerve
options.B: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs
options.C: It is too small to yield an adequate blood sample
options.D: It has thick muscular walls that resist needle entry

explanation: Be cautious with the basilic vein—major nerves and the brachial artery run right beside it, so care is needed to avoid accidental injury.

question: Why do patients with Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) often develop dark, pigmented skin?

options.A: The adrenal glands leak excess stored pigments directly into the blood
options.B: Dehydration causes the outer skin layers to thicken and darken
options.C: Poor kidney function traps waste products underneath the skin layers
options.D: The pituitary gland releases high amounts of ACTH, which stimulates melanin

explanation: When the adrenals fail to make enough cortisol, the brain panics and pumps out a flood of ACTH to try and wake them up. High ACTH accidentally triggers melanin (skin pigment) production too!

question: A nurse fills out a Yellow Form for a patient who got a rash after taking two new drugs and an herbal supplement. What should be included in the medication history?

options.A: Only document the drug that the nurse personally administered
options.B: List all prescribed drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products
options.C: Ignore the herbal supplement since it is not a pharmaceutical drug
options.D: Only list the most expensive brand-name prescription drug

explanation: Always list everything! Herbal remedies and over-the-counter items frequently cause or contribute to adverse reactions.

question: What is the main job of a skilled birth attendant during a home delivery?

options.A: To transport the mother to a hospital for every contraction
options.B: To prescribe long-term contraception before labor starts
options.C: To perform emergency cesarean sections in the home
options.D: To monitor mother and baby and manage normal childbirth

explanation: You've got this! A skilled birth attendant is simply there to watch how labor progresses, support the mother, and safely handle a normal delivery while keeping an eye out for any trouble.

question: If a patient has a stroke on the right side of their motor cortex, which side of the body will show physical weakness?

options.A: The right side
options.B: The left side
options.C: Only the lower limbs
options.D: Both sides equally

explanation: Brilliant! Brain pathways cross over in the brainstem, so damage on the right side of the brain shows up as weakness on the left side of the body.

question: What is an important nursing duty right after a client finishes their EEG?

options.A: Ensuring regular seizure medications are resumed promptly
options.B: Keeping the client awake for another twelve hours
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent water intoxication
options.D: Applying fresh adhesive paste back onto the scalp

explanation: If any regular meds (especially seizure meds) were paused for the test, make sure to get them back on board right away to keep the patient safe!

question: Why is keeping accurate records of swab counts so important for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It provides legal protection and proves adherence to safety standards
options.B: It replaces the need to count out loud in the theater
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy fewer supplies next year
options.D: It is only required for hospital billing departments

explanation: Good paperwork is your best backup! Clear records show you followed all safety rules and protect you legally.

question: What warning signs should you teach a patient to report right away after going home from a dilation?

options.A: Mild scratchy throat sensation
options.B: Slight fatigue from the sedation
options.C: Temporary change in voice pitch
options.D: Fever and severe worsening pain

explanation: A little throat scratchiness is totally normal after having tools passed down. But fever and severe, getting-worse pain mean infection or a tear, which need immediate care.

question: Why do blood vessels swell and open up wider during inflammation?

options.A: To prevent the complement proteins from entering the injury site
options.B: To lower local tissue temperature and stop bacterial growth
options.C: To allow white blood cells and fluid to move easily into infected tissues
options.D: To slow down local blood flow so pathogens can multiply and be counted

explanation: Spot on! Opening the blood vessels lets protective white blood cells and fluid rush straight to the injury or infection site.

question: What is the main goal of using disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs)?

options.A: To cure bacterial joint infections within a few days
options.B: To replace lost cartilage with artificial tissue instantly
options.C: To lower blood pressure during acute flare-ups
options.D: To slow down long-term immune-mediated joint damage

explanation: DMARDs help calm down an overactive immune system, protecting the joints from long-term, permanent destruction over time.

question: What is the best way to protect a PAC patient's privacy in a busy ward?

options.A: Transferring the client to an administrative office
options.B: Asking family members to step outside during visiting hours only
options.C: Placing a warning sign on the door of the main ward
options.D: Drawing bedside curtains and speaking in low, quiet tones

explanation: Simple steps like pulling the curtains tight and keeping your voice down stop nosey neighbors from hearing private health details.

question: How does good birth spacing directly help a child survive and stay healthy?

options.A: By automatically increasing household monthly income and food production
options.B: By eliminating the transmission of all known genetic disorders
options.C: By giving the mother's body time to recover and rebuild essential nutrient stores
options.D: By ensuring older siblings graduate from secondary school first

explanation: Spot on! When a mother's body gets enough time to rest and rebuild nutrients between pregnancies, she is stronger and better equipped to nourish her next baby.

question: Why do nurses treat early marriage as a serious public health issue?

options.A: Because it increases the workload of hospital administrative staff
options.B: Because it violates international trade agreements between countries
options.C: Because it directly causes severe physical, psychological, and obstetric complications
options.D: Because it prevents young couples from building modern houses

explanation: You got it! Young bodies aren't ready for childbearing, leading to deep health and emotional scars. That makes it a major healthcare concern.

question: Why is it risky to assume sudden confusion in an older adult is just 'normal aging'?

options.A: It automatically leads to permanent psychiatric institutionalization
options.B: It can cause nurses to miss acute illnesses like infections
options.C: It interferes with standard medication dosage calculations
options.D: It accelerates the natural hardening of the arteries

explanation: Great nursing insight! Never brush off sudden confusion as mere old age. It's often a red flag signaling a serious issue like a urinary tract infection or lack of oxygen.

question: Why do doctors order antibody blood tests like rheumatoid factor when checking joint pain?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys filter waste products
options.B: To measure the exact daily amount of calcium in the bones
options.C: To determine if the client has an active bacterial wound infection
options.D: To check for specific proteins that indicate an autoimmune attack

explanation: Tests like rheumatoid factor look for rogue proteins that show the immune system is mistakenly attacking the body's own healthy joint tissues.

question: What is a major cause of clinical errors when patients are being transferred between care teams?

options.A: Excessive time spent resting on duty
options.B: Overuse of basic patient hygiene supplies
options.C: Strict adherence to written safety checklists
options.D: Communication breakdowns during handovers

explanation: Spot on! Poor communication during shift changes or patient transfers often leads to missed details, making handovers a high-risk moment for mistakes.

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living.

question: Why are regular screening colonoscopies so good at preventing colorectal cancer?

options.A: They allow doctors to find and remove pre-cancerous polyps early
options.B: They prevent the body from absorbing dietary fats
options.C: They completely kill all harmful bacteria living inside the bowel
options.D: They strengthen the muscle wall of the descending colon

explanation: You nailed it! Finding and clipping out polyps during a routine check stops them from hanging around long enough to turn into cancer.

question: What is the job of pepsinogen once it is inside the stomach?

options.A: It converts into active pepsin to break down proteins
options.B: It lines the stomach wall to protect it from ulcers
options.C: It stimulates the release of bile from the liver
options.D: It neutralizes excess stomach acid

explanation: Chief cells release pepsinogen as a safe, inactive form. Once stomach acid hits it, it turns into active pepsin to start chopping up proteins! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h4)

question: How does Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) primarily help someone deal with anxiety?

options.A: By prescribing strong sedative medications for daily use
options.B: By using physical exercise to tire out the nervous system
options.C: By teaching the patient how to avoid all stressful life events
options.D: By replacing negative or distorted thoughts with realistic ones

explanation: CBT is all about catching those sneaky, unhelpful thought patterns and learning how to flip them into grounded, balanced perspectives.

question: What main feature separates hospital waste from ordinary rubbish at home?

options.A: It always smells much worse than domestic garbage
options.B: It is generated only by medical doctors and surgeons
options.C: It can be recycled directly without prior processing
options.D: It contains biological, chemical, and radioactive hazards

explanation: You got this! Healthcare waste needs special care because it carries dangerous germs and materials that can cause disease or injury—unlike normal house trash.

question: What is one of the earliest warning signs of hidden blood loss or developing shock?

options.A: A sudden drop in body weight
options.B: A gradual increase in heart rate
options.C: Deep and slow snoring
options.D: An increase in appetite

explanation: As fluid or blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to keep blood flowing to vital organs before blood pressure actually falls. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h4)

question: What role do descriptive studies play in nursing science?

options.A: They supply baseline facts that point toward areas needing clinical investigation
options.B: They replace clinical trials by proving which drugs cure diseases
options.C: They force patients to alter their daily health habits for better outcomes
options.D: They eliminate all errors found in previous medical journals

explanation: Descriptive studies act like our radar—they highlight where health issues lie, guiding nurses on what needs closer study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h2)

question: A doctor wants to know if a patient's low testosterone is due to a problem in the testes or the pituitary gland. Which test helps figure this out?

options.A: Serum LH and FSH hormone levels
options.B: A prostate-specific antigen blood test
options.C: A complete blood count with differential
options.D: A routine urinalysis and urine culture

explanation: Checking LH and FSH levels from the pituitary gland helps doctors see if the issue starts in the brain (pituitary) or down in the testes. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: When we classify a joint by its 'function', what are we actually describing?

options.A: How much movement the joint allows
options.B: The chemical makeup of its fluid
options.C: The muscles attached to it
options.D: How fast it heals after an injury

explanation: Exactly! Functional classification is simply about range of motion—whether the joint moves freely, a little bit, or not at all.

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis?

options.A: To kill all viruses while leaving bacteria alive
options.B: To reduce the total number of common bacteria
options.C: To eliminate every single microorganism and spore
options.D: To remove visible dirt and grease from the skin

explanation: You've got this! Surgical asepsis is all about absolute sterility—getting rid of every living germ and tough spore so nothing can cause infection.

question: Which environmental strategy helps manage a confused and restless patient experiencing delirium?

options.A: Playing loud, fast-paced music to keep their attention focused
options.B: Keeping the room quiet and well-lit with familiar personal items nearby
options.C: Restricting all family members from visiting to prevent stimulation
options.D: Constantly moving the patient to a brand new room every shift

explanation: A calm, recognizable environment reduces fear and disorientation in patients with altered mental status. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h6)

question: What must you do if an unsterile object accidentally touches your sterile field while setting up?

options.A: Throw away the whole field and set up a fresh sterile kit.
options.B: Spray antiseptic over the area and wait two minutes.
options.C: Wipe the spot with alcohol and keep going.
options.D: Ignore it if the object looked clean enough.

explanation: Safety first! If a sterile field is touched by something unsterile, its clean status is broken and you have to start fresh. Better safe than sorry in infection control.

question: Why do low-resource communities usually suffer the most from improper toxic waste dumping?

options.A: Warm climates cause toxic waste to evaporate completely into the upper atmosphere
options.B: They lack the robust infrastructure needed to detect and treat contamination
options.C: Local hospitals specialize in reversing the effects of heavy metal poisoning
options.D: Their residents willingly consume industrial chemicals for traditional remedies

explanation: You nailed it. Communities with fewer resources often struggle to test their water or provide medical care for long-term toxic exposure.

question: What is the primary goal of triage in an emergency department?

options.A: Sorting patients based on injury severity
options.B: Determining the patient's insurance status
options.C: Collecting payment before starting care
options.D: Registering patient names and addresses

explanation: Triage prioritizes care so that patients with the most life-threatening conditions receive immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why might a high fever temporarily lower a male patient's sperm count?

options.A: White blood cells consume all available nutrients inside the seminiferous tubules
options.B: Higher body temperature disrupts the cool environment needed for healthy sperm development
options.C: Infections directly destroy mature sperm cells stored inside the urinary bladder
options.D: Fever causes the pituitary gland to permanently stop producing testosterone

explanation: Remember, sperm love cooler temperatures! A high fever raises the temperature in the scrotum, which temporarily pauses or slows down normal sperm production.

question: What is the biggest clinical advantage of giving a medication straight into a vein (intravenously)?

options.A: It requires minimal monitoring compared to oral medications.
options.B: It prevents rapid allergic reactions from occurring.
options.C: It carries zero risk of localized tissue irritation.
options.D: It provides immediate systemic availability of the medication.

explanation: You're doing great! Since IV medications go right into the bloodstream, they start working instantly—a lifesaver in emergencies.

question: A patient asks if changing their diet and exercising can help with mild erectile dysfunction. What is the best response?

options.A: Once sexual dysfunction starts, lifestyle changes can never reverse it
options.B: Diet and exercise only affect heart disease and have no link to sexual function
options.C: You should stop exercising immediately to preserve your energy
options.D: Lifestyle changes improve blood circulation and can significantly benefit sexual health

explanation: Absolutely! What is good for the heart is good for sexual health. Better circulation means better physical function overall.

question: What is the main goal of gender-transformative nursing care?

options.A: To enforce traditional cultural rules without questioning them
options.B: To eliminate the study of biological sex differences entirely
options.C: To actively challenge harmful stereotypes and promote equality
options.D: To treat all patients using identical physical interventions

explanation: Brilliant! Gender-transformative care means speaking up against unequal power dynamics and harmful norms to help every patient achieve better health.

question: How does carrying excess body weight contribute directly to knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: It increases mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints and promotes inflammation
options.B: It stops the body from producing normal synovial fluid
options.C: It causes the leg muscles to weaken and shrink away completely
options.D: It blocks calcium from reaching the bone ends inside the joint

explanation: Extra weight forces the knee joints to bear heavier loads with every step, and fat tissue also releases chemicals that trigger joint inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: In health informatics, what does the abbreviation CPOE stand for?

options.A: Certified Practical Operations Expert
options.B: Computerized Provider Order Entry
options.C: Central Pharmacy Order Exchange
options.D: Clinical Patient Online Evaluation

explanation: CPOE is just the digital system doctors and other providers use to type their orders directly into the computer network.

question: Why is a patient scheduled for an abdominal ultrasound usually told to fast (no food or water) for a few hours beforehand?

options.A: To keep their blood pressure steady before the scan
options.B: To cut down on tummy gas and keep the gallbladder full
options.C: To make sure they have an empty bladder for a pelvic check
options.D: To stop them from throwing up during the procedure

explanation: Food creates gas that blocks sound waves, and fasting keeps the gallbladder nice and full so it's easy to see!

question: Why do waterborne diseases like cholera often spike during the rainy season in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Rainfall increases the population of adult malaria-carrying mosquitoes
options.B: Cold weather lowers overall human immunity against intestinal parasites
options.C: Heavy rains can wash surface waste and sewage into vulnerable drinking water sources
options.D: Humidity causes airborne bacteria to multiply rapidly in closed indoor spaces

explanation: Exactly right. Heavy floods easily mix surface waste into community water supplies, increasing the risk of waterborne illnesses.

question: What is the main goal of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: To safely bridge classroom theory with clinical practice
options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures completely
options.C: To reduce the number of hours spent in real hospitals
options.D: To test students so they can be ranked in their class

explanation: Simulation gives students a bridge between what they read in books and the realities of caring for patients, all without any risk of harm. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the normal adult blood range for potassium?

options.A: 95 to 105 mmol/L

options.D: 135 to 145 mmol/L

question: What is a major risk when hospital waste isn't disposed of properly in the community?

options.A: Faster patient discharge rates

options.D: Lower hospital utility bills

question: At what specific location do nerve fibers from the inside of each retina cross to the other side?

options.A: Occipital lobe

options.C: Optic disc
options.D: Optic chiasm

question: What is the main reason for writing a nursing diagnosis in a patient care plan?

options.A: To determine the total cost of hospital treatment
options.B: To replace the medical diagnosis given by the physician
options.C: To legally clear the nurse from liability
options.D: To guide the selection of appropriate nursing interventions

explanation: Correct! A nursing diagnosis highlights how the patient is responding to a health issue, which helps you decide what nursing actions to take next.

question: What is the main purpose of preparing a patient for community reintegration before hospital discharge?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital nursing staff
options.B: To test if the patient can survive without any medical supplies
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for health insurance
options.D: To ensure a smooth and safe transition back to home and daily routines

explanation: Community reintegration focuses on equipping the patient and home environment for real-world independence and participation. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h8)

question: What position is a female patient usually placed in for a full pelvic examination?

options.A: Prone position
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: Semi-Fowler position
options.D: Lithotomy position

explanation: Correct! The lithotomy position (lying on the back with legs in stirrups) gives you the best view and access for checking pelvic organs.

question: Why does the skin get very dark (hyperpigmentation) in primary Addison's disease?

options.A: Lack of cortisol stops the liver from breaking down skin pigments
options.B: Aldosterone deficiency directly stains the dermal layers of the skin
options.C: Dehydration causes melanin pigments to concentrate in surface tissues
options.D: The pituitary gland increases ACTH and melanocyte-stimulating hormone production

explanation: When the adrenal glands fail, the brain panics and sends out a flood of ACTH to wake them up. Because ACTH shares a chemical cousin that triggers skin pigment, the patient's skin starts to darken.

question: If someone has a metabolic acid-base problem, which organ system jumps in first to try and balance it out?

options.A: The respiratory system through changes in ventilation
options.B: The integumentary system through sweat production
options.C: The digestive system through gastric acid secretion
options.D: The endocrine system through hormone release

explanation: Your lungs are fast responders! By breathing faster or slower, they can blow off or trap carbon dioxide to help fix metabolic imbalances quickly.
